topic.title: Preface
topic.shortdesc: How this book came to be, who it is for, and how to get the most from it.

body.p: This book began as a test suite. When building the dita2epub pluginorigindita2epub plugin, I needed a sample publication that exercised every feature: cover pages and title pages, tables of contents and indexes, footnotes and glossaries, figures with captions and tables with zebra striping. Rather than create a minimal, throwaway fixture, I decided to write a real book — one that would serve as both documentation and integration test.

The result is the volume you are reading now. Every element on every page is generated by the plugin it describes. If the footnotes workLike this one., it is because the footnote template works. If the index at the back points to the right pages, it is because the indexing pipeline works. The book is its own test report.

section.title: Who This Book Is For
section.p: This book is written for three audiences:

ul.li: Technical writers who author content in DITAauthoringDITA and want to produce EPUB 3 output. You will learn how to structure your bookmap, configure the transformation, and take advantage of features like font embedding, image optimization, and accessibility metadata.

Documentation managers who are evaluating tools for digital publishing. The feature comparison tables and parameter reference in the appendices will help you assess whether this plugin meets your requirements.
Developers who want to extend or customize the plugin. The architecture overview in Chapter 1 and the element reference in Appendix B provide the technical detail you need.

section.title: How This Book Is Organized
section.p: The book follows a traditional structure that itself exercises the bookmap features of the plugin:

dlentry.dd: The dedication, foreword, this preface, acknowledgments, and introduction. These pages test the plugin's handling of front-matter topic types, including the automatic assignment of DPUB-ARIA roles like doc-foreword and doc-preface.
Covers the basics of DITA, EPUB 3, and the transformation pipeline. Includes installation instructions, first-run examples, and an overview of how DITA elements map to EPUB structures.
Explores font embedding, image optimization, accessibility compliance, and best practices for metadata. This is where the plugin's advanced features are demonstrated in depth.

A visual tour of every supported DITA element: notes, code blocks, tables with column spans, figures, blockquotes, sidebars, and footnotes. This chapter exists primarily to stress-test the rendering pipeline.

An afterword, two appendices (parameter reference and element reference), release notes, bibliography, colophon, glossary, and index. Each of these exercises a distinct back-matter feature of the plugin.

section.title: Conventions
section.p: The following typographic conventions are used throughout:

ul.li: Monospace text indicates parameter names, file paths, XML element names, and command-line input.
Bold text highlights important terms when they are first introduced.
Italic text is used for emphasis, publication titles, and attributed quotations.

section.note: Notes like this one provide supplementary advice, shortcuts, or background information. They are color-coded by type: blue for general notes, green for tips, orange for warnings, red for important alerts, and dark red for danger notices.

section.title: Source Code and Feedback
section.p: The complete DITA source for this book, along with the plugin itself, is available on GitHub at github.com/jyjeanne/dita2epub. Issues, feature requests, and pull requests are welcome.
